extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for determining when and how a U.S. patent, U.S. patent application publication, or WIPO PCT publication is usable as prior art under the pre-AIA version of 35 U.S.C. 102(e), including how to compute the applicable prior-art date and when provisional rejections over unpublished/copending applications are permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualifying reference types for pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(e)
rubrics_metrics.description: Only certain references may be applied under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(e): a U.S. patent, a U.S. application publication (35 U.S.C. 122(b)), or a WIPO publication of an international application under PCT Article 21(2) (in English where applicable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A SIR (statutory invention registration) published under former 35 U.S.C. 157(c) is treated the same as a U.S. patent for defensive purposes and is usable as a 102(e) reference as of its filing date. If a publication/issue date is too recent for 102(a)/(b), 102(e) may still be used if filing-date conditions are met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior-art date when reference did not result from or claim benefit of an IA
rubrics_metrics.description: If the potential reference did not result from, nor claim the benefit of, an international application, its pre-AIA 102(e) prior art date is its earliest effective U.S. filing date, taking into account any proper benefit claims to earlier U.S. applications under 35 U.S.C. 119(e) or 120.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For benefit claims, the prior application(s) must properly support the subject matter used to make the rejection in compliance with pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 112 (first paragraph) / 35 U.S.C. 112(a). For 119(e) provisional benefit claims see the separate provisional-support requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: When an international filing date is treated as a U.S. filing date (IA on/after Nov 29, 2000)
rubrics_metrics.description: An international filing date of an international application (IA) filed on or after November 29, 2000 is a U.S. filing date for pre-AIA 102(e) prior art purposes only if: (a) the IA has an international filing date on or after Nov 29, 2000; (b) the IA designated the United States; and (c) the IA was published by WIPO under PCT Article 21(2) in the English language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If these three conditions are met, the IA filing date (or an earlier effective U.S. filing date to which the IA properly claims benefit) is the 102(e) date, provided all requirements for benefit claims (119(e), 120, 365(c), 386(c)) and 112 written-description support are satisfied.

rubrics_metrics.name: IA filed on/after Nov 29, 2000 but failing designation or English publication
rubrics_metrics.description: If the IA was filed on or after Nov 29, 2000 but did not designate the United States or was not published in English under PCT Article 21(2), do not treat the international filing date as a U.S. filing date for pre-AIA 102(e) purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In this situation the reference may be applied under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(a) or 102(b) as of its publication date, or under 102(e) as of any later U.S. filing date of an application that properly claims the benefit of the IA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of international applications filed prior to Nov 29, 2000
rubrics_metrics.description: International applications filed prior to Nov 29, 2000 are governed by pre-AIPA provisions: for U.S. patents that result from such IAs, apply the reference under pre-AIA 102(e) as of the earlier of the date of completion of the requirements of 35 U.S.C. 371(c)(1),(2) and (4) or the filing date of the later-filed U.S. application that claimed the benefit of the IA. Application publications from such IAs do not have a pre-AIA 102(e) date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Application publications (WIPO or U.S.) of IAs filed prior to Nov 29, 2000 may be applied under pre-AIA 102(a) or 102(b) as of their publication dates, but never under 102(e). If a U.S. application publication claims benefit under 120/365(c) of such an IA, apply 102(e) as of the actual filing date of the later-filed U.S. application claiming the benefit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Benefit-claim subject-matter support requirement (112 compliance)
rubrics_metrics.description: For any benefit claim (35 U.S.C. 119(e), 120, 365(c), 386(c)) used to secure an earlier effective filing date for a reference under pre-AIA 102(e), the subject matter relied upon in the rejection must be disclosed in the earlier-filed application in compliance with pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 112 (first paragraph) / 35 U.S.C. 112(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners must verify written-description/support in the earlier application for the specific subject matter used to make the rejection before attributing the earlier filing date to the reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional (35 U.S.C. 119(e)) benefit — claim-support special rule
rubrics_metrics.description: A benefit claim under 35 U.S.C. 119(e) to a provisional application gives the potential reference the provisional filing date for 102(e) purposes only if at least one claim of the potential reference is supported by the written description of the provisional application in compliance with pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 112 (first paragraph) / 35 U.S.C. 112(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners must check that at least one claim in the reference reads on subject matter supported by the provisional's written description before using the provisional's filing date as the 102(e) date. See MPEP § 2136.03, subsection III for more detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventive-entity requirement for applying pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(e)
rubrics_metrics.description: To apply a reference under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(e), the inventive entity of the application under examination must be different from that of the cited reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where there are joint inventors, only one inventor needs to be different for inventive entities to be considered different; thus a 102(e) rejection may be appropriate even if some inventors are in common between the application and the cited reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent 'granted' requirement and validity not required
rubrics_metrics.description: For pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(e)(2) to apply to a patent, the statute requires that the patent be 'granted', but it does not require that the patent be currently valid to be applied under 102(e)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An issued patent may be used as prior art under 102(e)(2) even if it is later found invalid. (See cited case Becton, Dickinson & Co. v. Baxter Corp. Englewood.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign priority claims (35 U.S.C. 119(a)-(d)) not effective for 102(e)
rubrics_metrics.description: A U.S. application (35 U.S.C. 111(a)) that claims priority under 35 U.S.C. 119(a)-(d) to a prior foreign-filed application is accorded its U.S. filing date as its pre-AIA 102(e) prior art date — no benefit of the foreign filing date is given under pre-AIA 102(e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: an application with a foreign priority claim will have the U.S. filing date as its 102(e) date (In re Hilmer).

rubrics_metrics.name: Status of unpublished or redacted copending U.S. applications with no common assignee/applicant/inventor
rubrics_metrics.description: If there is no common assignee, applicant, or inventor, and the earlier-filed application was not published under 35 U.S.C. 122(b), the earlier unpublished application (or subject matter not supported in a redacted publication) remains confidential and cannot be relied upon as prior art under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such an earlier-filed application must be allowed to issue (or be published) before it can be used as a 102(e) reference. If filing dates are within interference timeframes, consider interference practice (MPEP Chapter 2300).

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional pre-AIA 102(e) rejection permitted when common assignee/applicant/inventor
rubrics_metrics.description: When there is at least one common inventor or applicant between copending applications (or they are commonly assigned) and the effective filing dates differ, an examiner may provisionally reject a later-filed application under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(e) over an earlier-filed, unpublished application (or a redacted publication where the relied-upon subject matter is not shown).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A provisional rejection puts applicant on early notice of possible prior-art relationship and may be overcome in the same manner as a standard 102(e) rejection (e.g., amendment, evidence, abandonment and refiling). Use form paragraph 7.15.01.fti for provisional 102(e) rejections. Provisional rejections are authorized only when there is a common inventor or assignee; otherwise confidentiality must be maintained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional-rejection and examination procedure notes
rubrics_metrics.description: Provisional rejections under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(e) are appropriate where the earlier-filed application is expected to ripen into a patent or publication and would constitute actual prior art if later issued/published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provisional 102(e) rejections serve to maximize applicant's opportunity to overcome the rejection and are handled like final 102(e) rejections for purposes of response; they can also be addressed by the applicant abandoning or refiling a combined application. See MPEP § 2136.05 and § 2146.03(a) (provisional rejections under 103 using provisional prior art).
